answer: Price identity in dedicated, unshareable storage. Each identity fills a large dataset seeded from its own key — so no two fakes hold the same bytes — and proves retention each epoch by answering random retrievability challenges that read back specific offsets. One honest agent dedicates one opal-slab of disk. A farm running a thousand fakes must physically store a thousand distinct datasets at once and pass a thousand independent audits, with no karst cavern of shared bytes to multiplex, since per-key uniqueness forbids one pearl of data standing in for many.
